newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Clinton sends letter to PLO's Arafat.
newsitem.headline: Clinton sends letter to PLO's Arafat.

text.p: U.S. President Bill Clinton sent a letter to Palestinian President Yasser Arafat on Friday, one day before an international meeting on Middle East peace moves in Gaza, the Voice of Palestine Radio said.
It said the U.S. consul general in Jerusalem, Edward Abington, delivered the letter to Arafat in the West Bank town of Bethlehem shortly before the PLO leader returned to Gaza.
U.S. and Palestinian officials were not immediately available to comment on the report.
The radio gave no details on the contents of the letter, which arrived a day after a Jordanian soldier shot dead seven Israeli schoolgirls touring a Jordanian border site.

Arafat has called a meeting of U.S., European and Arab envoys for Saturday in Gaza that he says is needed to save the Middle East peace process from a crisis over Israeli plans to build a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem.
Washington has said it would send Abington.
In Washington on Thursday, House of Representatives Republican leaders led by Speaker Newt Gingrich told Clinton that U.S. participation in the Gaza conference was a mistake.
They said that by agreeing to take part, Washington was sending a message that it was possible to drive a wedge between the United States and Israel.
Thursday's attack put pressure on the United States to broker a swift end to the crisis in Israeli-Arab relations over the plans for the 6,500-apartment Jewish settlement.
The U.S. State Department has said it is appropriate for Arafat to "talk to friendly countries around the world".
